source_evidence: Series I U.S. Savings Bonds are inflation-indexed. They are sold at face value and you can buy up to $10,000 (face value) of Series I bonds in any calendar year. Series I Bonds offer a fixed rate of interest, adjusted for inflation.
answer: Series I savings bonds are designed to account for inflation: they offer a fixed interest rate that is adjusted for inflation. They are sold at face value, and the source states that an individual can buy up to $10,000 in Series I bonds in a calendar year.
